quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #18
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 18

questions.question: What is distracted driving?

options.text: Anything that causes you to swerve while driving.
Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
Anything that makes you focus more on driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
questions.explanation: Distracted driving means doing something that takes your eyes, hands, or mind away from driving. It is the most common cause of traffic accidents. Any distraction can cause you to miss important signs and sounds that help you avoid crashes.

questions.question: How can you prevent hydroplaning?

options.text: Keep your tire tread in good condition.
Keep your tires filled to the correct pressure.
Slow down when it rains.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: To prevent hydroplaning, keep your tires in good condition with proper tread and correct air pressure. Slow down when driving in the rain. Hydroplaning happens most often at high speeds.

questions.question: When turning, you must ____ your speed.

options.text: Increase
Keep the same
Change
Reduce

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce
questions.explanation: When turning, slow down to a speed where you can control your vehicle, stay in your lane, and handle unexpected situations.

questions.question: When should you use your horn?

options.text: When another vehicle is in your way.
When it can help prevent a crash.
When another driver makes a mistake.

questions.correctAnswerText: When it can help prevent a crash.
questions.explanation: Use your horn only when needed to avoid a crash. Do not use it to tell a driver or cyclist to go faster or move out of your way.

questions.question: You are entering an interstate highway. What should you do?

options.text: Find a safe gap and merge into traffic.
Merge across two lanes at the same time.
Always stop before entering the highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Find a safe gap and merge into traffic.
questions.explanation: When merging, find a gap wide enough to safely enter traffic. Do not stop on the entrance ramp unless there is no safe gap to merge into.

questions.question: The driver ahead stops at a crosswalk. What should you do?

options.text: Pass the vehicle slowly at 10 mph or less.
Stop and wait until all pedestrians have crossed.
Change lanes and pass the stopped vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and wait until all pedestrians have crossed.
questions.explanation: Never pass a vehicle stopped at a crosswalk. There may be pedestrians you cannot see. Stop and only move when all pedestrians have finished crossing.

questions.question: A child is riding a bicycle near your vehicle. What should you do?

options.text: Honk your horn.
Trust that the child has full control of the bike.
Be prepared for anything.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be prepared for anything.
questions.explanation: Children on bikes are unpredictable and may change direction suddenly. Children and bicycles are small and can be hard to see.

questions.question: It is illegal to drive in the same lane as a motorcycle.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: True
questions.explanation: Never share a lane with a motorcycle, even if there appears to be room. Motorcycles need the full lane width to move safely.

questions.question: You see a large puddle on the road ahead. What should you do?

options.text: Keep your speed to drive through the water.
Stay away from the puddle if you can.
Shift into neutral while driving through the water.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay away from the puddle if you can.
questions.explanation: Avoid slippery areas like ice, wet leaves, oil, and deep puddles. Dry, solid surfaces are safest for driving.

questions.question: A yellow traffic light means the red light is coming. If you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow, what should you do?

options.text: Stop.
Continue through and clear the intersection safely.
Speed up to avoid causing an accident.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue through and clear the intersection safely.
questions.explanation: If you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow, continue through and clear the intersection as quickly as possible.

questions.question: If you stop along the road at night, what should you do?

options.text: Turn off all your lights.
Use your parking lights only.
Use your headlights only.
Turn on your emergency flashers and leave your low beams on.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your emergency flashers and leave your low beams on.
questions.explanation: When you stop on the road at night, turn on your emergency flashers and keep your low beams on. This helps other drivers see your vehicle.

questions.question: When you drive where children are playing, what should you expect?

options.text: They will know when it is safe to cross.
They will stop at the curb before crossing.
They will run out in front of you without looking.
They will not cross unless an adult is with them.

questions.correctAnswerText: They will run out in front of you without looking.
questions.explanation: Slow down and be careful when children are nearby. They may not understand danger and could run in front of your car without looking.

questions.question: Distracted driving is:

options.text: Very uncommon.
Extremely risky behavior.
Nothing to worry about.
Just as safe as normal driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Extremely risky behavior.
questions.explanation: Distracted driving is very dangerous. It puts you, your passengers, and other people on the road at risk. Paying full attention while driving helps prevent crashes.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Four-lane traffic ahead.
Divided highway ahead.
Two-way traffic ahead.
Intersection ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Two-way traffic ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that traffic is coming in both directions.

questions.question: When an emergency vehicle with flashing lights is near you, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up to get out of the way.
Stop your vehicle right away and block their path.
Do everything you can to give them a clear path.
Signal to them when it is safe to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do everything you can to give them a clear path.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle with flashing lights is nearby, make space for it to pass. If it is safe, pull to the side of the road to let them through.

questions.question: A U-turn is not allowed:

options.text: In a parking lot.
On or near a curve or hill.
On a straight road with a clear view for 500 feet in both directions.

questions.correctAnswerText: On or near a curve or hill.
questions.explanation: Never make a U-turn on or near a curve or hill. You cannot see oncoming traffic or pedestrians, which could cause a crash.

questions.question: When turning onto a street with multiple lanes in your direction, which lane should you turn into?

options.text: The lane closest to your previous lane.
The lane marked with an arrow.
The middle lane.
Any lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane closest to your previous lane.
questions.explanation: Turn into the lane that is closest to the lane you are coming from. Do not switch lanes while turning.

questions.question: What do speed limit signs show?

options.text: Suggested speeds for the area.
The highest or lowest speed allowed by law.
The speed to drive in heavy traffic.
The speed to drive in bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: The highest or lowest speed allowed by law.
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs show the highest or lowest speed you are allowed to drive. The posted speed is for good conditions. You must slow down when conditions are bad.

questions.question: When driving in fog, use your low beam headlights.

options.text: TRUE
FALSE

questions.correctAnswerText: TRUE
questions.explanation: Use your low beams in fog. High beams reflect off the fog and shine back into your eyes, making it harder to see.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Sharp right turn ahead.
A road joins from the right.
The road turns sharply right, then sharply left.
Winding road ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road turns sharply right, then sharply left.
questions.explanation: This sign means the road ahead has a sharp right turn followed by a sharp left turn.

questions.question: When turning left from a multilane one-way street onto another one-way street, which lane should you start from?

options.text: Any lane, as long as it is safe.
The lane closest to the left curb.
The center lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane closest to the left curb.
questions.explanation: When turning left from a one-way street to another one-way street, start your turn from the far left lane.

questions.question: What does a flashing red light on a traffic signal mean?

options.text: It means the same thing as a stop sign.
The traffic signal is broken.
You do not have to come to a complete stop.
Driving conditions are dangerous.

questions.correctAnswerText: It means the same thing as a stop sign.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same thing as a stop sign. Stop completely, yield to other traffic and pedestrians, and only go when it is safe.

questions.question: What do double solid yellow lane markings mean?

options.text: Neither lane may pass.
Both lanes may pass.
The right lane may pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Neither lane may pass.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow markings separate traffic going in opposite directions. Passing is not allowed from either direction.

questions.question: What should you do when entering a roadway from a private road?

options.text: Use your horn to warn other drivers.
Stop with part of your car on the roadway to alert drivers.
Drive out fast to merge smoothly with traffic.
Yield to pedestrians and traffic on the roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to pedestrians and traffic on the roadway.
questions.explanation: When entering a roadway from a driveway or private road, you must yield the right-of-way to pedestrians and all traffic on the roadway.

questions.question: What should you do if you have a tire blowout?

options.text: Tap or pump the brakes.
Slow down gradually and use your brakes lightly.
Apply the brakes firmly and quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down gradually and use your brakes lightly.
questions.explanation: During a tire blowout, slow down gradually by releasing the accelerator. Use your brakes lightly until the vehicle slows down significantly.
